title: Finite unramified Isom schemes for stable families over arbitrary bases
statement: Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $g\geq2$, and let $C\to T$ and $D\to T$ be stable unpointed genus-$g$ families in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. The functor on $T$-schemes sending $T'\to T$ to the set of $T'$-isomorphisms $C_{T'}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{T'}$ is represented by a finite unramified $T$-scheme $I_T(C,D)$. Its representing bijections commute with arbitrary base change and identify the universal point with a universal isomorphism of the two pulled-back curves. There is no field-base, finite-type, Noetherian, normality or reducedness hypothesis on $T$. The functor includes all disconnected and nonreduced test schemes. Finite means affine and finite as an algebra module on every affine chart [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; unramified means locally of finite type with diagonal an open immersion [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Pullbacks are scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 0DSQ (lemma-curves-diagonal-separated-fp), Tag 0E7A (lemma-stable-curves-deligne-mumford), Tag 0E9A (lemma-stable-separated): stable diagonal is proper and unramified, hence finite; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0418 (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-separated-representable), and spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 0A4X (lemma-characterize-finite) for the finite scheme realization.

proof.text: Cover $T$ by affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The restrictions of $C,D$ are proper by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper], and are flat finitely presented curve families by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve]. By [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine], $U$ is the inverse limit of the spectra $S_i$ of finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras of $A$. This is a small directed system (its rings form a subset of the power set of $A$), with affine transitions. Apply the object-descent clause of [lem-sfb-curve-limit-preservation] twice and pass to a common stage $i$. Obtain proper flat finitely presented algebraic-space curve families $C_i,D_i$ over $S_i$ and chosen identifications of their pullbacks to $U$ with $C_U,D_U$. These initial families need not be stable.

source.place: Tag 0D55 (lemma-curves-limits), object descent; affine Noetherian approximation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-arithmetic-stable-open-bounded] to each descended family, and let $S\subseteq S_i$ be the intersection of their stable genus-$g$ opens. The map $U\to S_i$ factors through both opens, hence through $S$, because its two pulled-back families are the original stable families. Over $S$ both $C_i,D_i$ are schemes and stable families in exactly the projective-bundle convention required here. The stage $S_i$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since it is of finite type over $\mathbf Z$; its open $S$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Replace the stage families by their restrictions $C_S,D_S$. No eventual stability on an entire affine stage is asserted or needed.

Use [lem-sfb-labelled-stable-isom-unramified] over the locally Noetherian scheme $S$, with $n=0$ and its unique permutation. This gives a separated finite-type unramified scheme $J\to S$ representing all isomorphisms between $C_S,D_S$, naturally on all $S$-schemes. There are no marking equations when $n=0$. For a DVR square $\operatorname{Spec}K\to J$, $\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$, naturality identifies the top arrow with a $K$-isomorphism of the two pulled-back stable families. By [lem-sfb-stable-labelled-isom-trait-extension] this extends to exactly one $R$-isomorphism. The representing bijection identifies it with exactly one lift $\operatorname{Spec}R\to J$ of the square, including the prescribed generic restriction. Thus [lem-sfb-noetherian-dvr-properness] makes $J\to S$ proper. Its finite-type hypothesis comes from the Isom lemma; no excellence or smooth generic-fibre hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 0E9A (lemma-stable-separated), diagonal properness; expanded using the existing persistently nodal trait-extension node and limits.tex Tag 0208 (lemma-Noetherian-dvr-valuative-proper).

proof.text: Since $J\to S$ is unramified, [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points] makes it locally quasi-finite. Apply [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite] to its properness from step 3 to conclude that $J\to S$ is finite. Put $I_U=J\times_SU$. The finite and unramified base-change clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] and [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open] show that $I_U\to U$ is finite unramified.

source.place: Tag 02LS (lemma-characterize-finite), proper locally quasi-finite implies finite; morphisms.tex Tags 02V5, 01W2, 02GA for quasi-finiteness and base change.

proof.text: For every $V\to U$, the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies maps $V\to I_U$ over $U$ with maps $V\to J$ over $S$. The natural representing bijection of [lem-sfb-labelled-stable-isom-unramified], followed by conjugation by the chosen pullback identifications from step 1, identifies these with $\operatorname{Isom}_V(C_V,D_V)$. The two identifications are natural in $V$. In particular $I_U$ represents the required functor on every $U$-scheme, with no reducedness or connectedness restriction.

source.place: Tag 0DSQ (lemma-curves-diagonal-separated-fp), interpretation by Isom functors; elementary fibre-product identification of the pulled-back representative.

proof.text: On any overlap $U\cap U'$ the two restricted representatives have naturally identical functors, by step 5. Apply [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] in the category of schemes over this overlap to the identity natural transformation and its inverse: obtain mutually inverse scheme maps. On triple overlaps their composites agree because they induce the same identity transformation; faithfulness gives the cocycle. This reasoning works on the actual open overlaps, which need not be affine. Now [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] glues the $I_U$ to a scheme $I$. Their structure maps to $T$ agree on overlaps and glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to $I\to T$, with $I\times_TU\simeq I_U$.

source.place: Scheme gluing along open overlaps; the canonical overlap maps are supplied by categories.tex Tag 001P (lemma-yoneda).

proof.text: Given any $V\to T$, cover $V$ by the inverse images $V_U$ of the chosen opens $U$. A map $V\to I$ gives isomorphisms $C_{V_U}\to D_{V_U}$ by step 5, agreeing on overlaps by the definition of the gluing maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to these maps on the open cover of $C_V$, and separately to their inverses on $D_V$. The composites are identity locally, hence globally by uniqueness in the same lemma. This constructs a $V$-isomorphism. Conversely a $V$-isomorphism gives compatible local maps $V_U\to I_U\subseteq I$, which glue uniquely. These operations are inverse and commute with every pullback, since they do so on each $V_U$ and the gluings are unique. Thus $I$ represents the required functor, including disconnected and nonreduced tests.

source.place: Gluing morphisms on open covers, applied both to isomorphisms and their inverses; elementary assembly of the local representing bijections.

proof.text: Finiteness of $I\to T$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target], applied to the affine covering used above. Unramifiedness follows from [lem-sfb-scheme-unramified-etale-locality]: at a point of $I_U$ use the open charts $I_U\to I$, $U\to T$, which are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and the unramified map $I_U\to U$. For any $T'\to T$ and $V\to T'$, [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies maps $V\to I\times_TT'$ over $T'$ with maps $V\to I$ over $T$, and hence with $\operatorname{Isom}_V(C_V,D_V)$ by step 7. This proves arbitrary-base-change compatibility. Evaluate the representing bijection at $V=I$ and $\mathrm{id}_I$ to obtain the universal isomorphism; naturality says its pullback along any $V\to I$ is the corresponding isomorphism. The empty base is handled by the empty cover and empty representative.

source.place: Tags 0DSQ, 0E7A, 0E9A: assembly of finite unramified arbitrary-base Isom representation; naturality gives the universal point and base change.

proof_origin.place: Arithmetic version of Tags 0DSQ, 0E7A, 0E9A, expanded by affine Noetherian approximation and the existing nodal trait-extension proof, rather than assuming a field base.
